Half of All US Employees Quit Their Jobs To Get Away From Bad Bosses: And Their Bosses Aren't Too Happy, Either

It makes sense. When I think of all the reasons why I left a job: boredom, under-pay, stress, environment, harassment, etc. My first course of action was to communicate my problems with my direct supervisor. When my supervisor did nothing, I labeled them a bad boss, and moved on to the next job. When my supervisor did something about it, or at least had a sympathetic conversation with me about it, I viewed them as a good boss.

The real story, is that a large number of companies are unable to find an adequate number of skilled and productive employees. This is because the free market has positioned itself in a way that has drastically reduced labor mobility. The cost of entering a new profession is so high, that most people stay at jobs they don't want to do. This "unfulfilled" workforce, is less able to synergize, and more sensitive to workplace stresses. If companies want to rectify this situation, instead of enforcing a regimented work place (suits, time clocks, cubicles) They should take a cue from companies like Google, Microsoft and Apple, who focus on building a workplace community, instead of a job.

The vice president got rid of the "team leader" position and moved all the team leaders (about 18 of them) and moved them up to "supervisors". We have certain jobs that are classified as "critical", and if you mess up once, you're automatically fired. She decided to put me on three of them at the same time. The stress I was under was immense, but I kept on keeping on for about two weeks.

I finally got called into HR one day, and the HR person said that she had heard that I had been insubordinate. While she was talking, she slid a paper across to me, and told me to fill out the questionnaire and sign it. So I did and we talked about what my supervisor had been doing to me. At the end, I signed the questionnaire, and she told me to clean out my locker. I asked why, and apparently I filled out the "exit form", and I had basically been tricked into quitting so I wouldn't be able to get unemployment.
